correctness.rationale: For all \(a\geq0\), interior node balance enforces equal path sine flows. Saturated flow has zero Hessian; every nonsaturated phase branch with negative path cosines has an explicitly constructed vector giving negative quadratic form, so strict stability requires three equal acute phase gaps. Its Hessian is positive modulo global phase exactly when \(\cos t>0\) and \(\cos t+3a\cos(3t)>0\). Maximizing the exact cubic \(F_a(s)=(1+3a)s-4as^3\) on [-1,1] gives the two threshold regimes. An increasing-branch solution exists strictly above the threshold. Differentiation yields the unique maximum and crossover. The extracted standalone checker passed 526 finite diagnostics, not substituted for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The user-relevant gap is the reliability of local Braess indicators when a link is added at finite weight, raised by the 2026 sensitivity work. This natural four-oscillator path-to-cycle construction yields a complete sharp analytic answer, including the onset of a new limiting phase branch at \(a=1/9\), worst penalty at \(a=1/6\), and a provable reversal at \(a\approx0.408894\). Those are physically interpretable structural thresholds not furnished by the local derivative or old endpoint inequalities. The result is self-contained, permits exact parameter selection, and remains interesting without a network-wide generalization. Although the open path is multiply marginal, the analytically sharp finite-weight reversal answers the distinct design question beyond first-order local assessment.
